World.title: Refugees, Migrants Tell of ‘Merciless’ Mass Beatings at Bulgarian Detention Centre
World.content:
Before the alleged violence, activists say protests had been going on for weeks against conditions at Pastrogor and the act of detention.

According to Collettivo Rotte Balcaniche, “in reaction, at least one person was beaten up by a police officer, detained at the police station, and forced to sign a pledge not to take part in any future protests”.

The situation came to a head on July 26, when Collettivo Rotte Balcaniche organised a demonstration outside the centre. Refugees and migrants joined in from inside.

One of the videos seen by BIRN shows nine migrants in a small room screaming “open camp” and a number of activists standing on top of a car near the perimeter of the facility. The protest was peaceful, the activists say.

Speaking on condition of anonymity, a Moroccan detainee told BIRN that two men – from Turkey and Tunisia – escaped. Other sources confirmed this.

“Then a policeman came and spoke to me in English, telling me to tell my friends to go back to their rooms upstairs because the rapid response team was coming, and if they found us in the square, things would get worse,” the Moroccan man said. “Everyone understood the situation. It was dangerous, so we returned to our rooms quietly.”

It is unclear which police unit the man meant by ‘rapid response team’. However, descriptions offered by migrants and refugees suggest the officers may have been part of the Bulgarian Gendarmerie.

According to BIRN sources inside the detention centre, the officers were dressed in full anti-riot gear, with masks, batons and stun guns. They were accompanied by regular policemen. The sources say there were around 30 to 40 in total.

“My friend and I were in the first room,” the Moroccan man said. “One of the masked men, holding a weapon, opened the door and said, ‘Get down! Get down!’ When I laid down on the floor, about 15 policemen entered the room and started beating us with batons. I thought it was the end. They beat me until I lost consciousness. They injured my friend’s head. They beat us mercilessly. I’ve never been beaten like that in my life. They went through all the rooms like that.”

Two other detainees, from Morocco and Pakistan, confirmed the account.

All sources BIRN spoke to stressed that beatings were meted out indiscriminately, across the facility. Collettivo Rotte Balcaniche said that surveillance cameras were turned off before the violence began, but offered no evidence.

‘Drenched in blood’

The second Moroccan man said officers also destroyed any phone they found, “so that we don’t publish photos of the beating”.

But images and videos have emerged.

Those seen by BIRN show at least eight different people with serious injuries, including two with bleeding head wounds. One man was drenched in blood.

The Pakistani detainee said he knew of at least 18 injured.

“They treated us brutally, as if we were criminals and not asylum seekers,” he said, speaking, like the others, on condition of anonymity.

After the beatings, the first Moroccan man said he and 11 other people were taken outside. “They started hitting and cursing and pouring water on us,” he said. “I felt hysterical, I felt like I was suffocating.”

He said the physical and verbal abuse continued at a nearby police station until the following day.

“They said, ‘If you don’t like the food, don’t eat it. Don’t do this. Don’t speak.’ They forced us to sign pledges and told us, ‘If you don’t like this treatment, go back to your country.’”

‘European standards’

World.title: Turkey Welcomes PKK Disarmament Law Despite Fears About Its Misuse
World.content:
Turkey last week took its most concrete legal step yet towards ending more than four decades of conflict with the Kurdistan Workers’ Party, PKK.

But while this is generating a rare political consensus and cautious optimism, suspicions about the intentions of the government overseeing the process run deep.

For many Kurds and other critics of the government, the central question is not only whether the PKK will disarm.

It is whether this process will lead to greater democracy, freedom and equal citizenship – or whether President Recep Tayyip Erdogan will use an initiative clothed in the language of peace to consolidate his own power.

World.title: Proposed Legal Changes to ‘Limit Rights’ Send Chill Through Serbian Schools
World.content:
As president of the Forum of Belgrade Gymnasiums, which represents grammar school employees in the Serbian capital, Ana Dimitrijevic attended a ‘public debate’ on August 5 at which Serbia’s education ministry opened discussion on a string of amendments that it wants to make to the Law on the Foundation of the Education System.

The ministry officials portrayed the amendments as “cosmetic”, Dimitrijevic recalled. They were anything but.

“They mostly underestimated our intelligence by explaining basic things we all know very well and pretended they didn’t understand why the fuss, when the amendments are cosmetic and not so important,” Dimitrijevic told BIRN. “When we asked for precise definitions of some of the amendments, they said ‘It goes without saying’, even though we all know it doesn’t.”

After more than 18 months of open confrontation between Serbia’s government and its educational institutions, from secondary schools to universities, the education ministry chose the summer holiday period to unveil legal changes that education workers fear will limit the ability of staff, pupils and parents to take a stand against social injustice.

They will broaden the grounds for teaching licences to be revoked, limit children’s right to assembly in school and reduce parental participation in the education system.

World.title: Albania Ruling Party Documents Highlight Country’s Ageing Demographic
World.content:
Documents produced by governing Socialist Party experts for a reform of the country’s municipal set-up, seen by BIRN, reveal an ageing population that could have adverse economic consequences for Albania.

The “Administrative-Territorial Reform 2.0” documents, prepared by experts on a special parliamentary committee, also show how emigration and internal migration have emptied out small towns and rural areas while concentrating the population in a few urban centres.

At one end are several urban centres where both population and economic activity are increasingly concentrated. At the other end are peripheral areas, particularly in the northeast, southeast and mountainous regions, which are caught in a vicious cycle of population decline and subsistence economies, with few formal jobs.

In these areas, municipal budgets survive largely on central government transfers, with funds often used mainly to cover the salaries of local administration staff.

The Urban Mass Index, UMI, one of three analytical documents underpinning the proposed new map of 46 municipalities – which would merge 15 local government units with larger municipalities – documents the territorial transformation of Albania since the 1990s, with a few centres continuing to grow as an increasing number of municipalities lose residents.

The “dependency ratio” in the index, which measures the burden that children and elderly people place on the working-age population, shows that in 51 municipalities out of 61 in total, this burden is higher than the national average. In many of them, the number of elderly residents exceeds the number of children.

The data highlights an Albania divided into three distinct realities: a small group of municipalities that continue to attract population and economic activity; a group of municipalities with intermediate potential; and a majority of the country’s territory, which is losing the critical mass of population needed to sustain local economies and public services.

The analysis is based on data from the 2023 census and, as part of the technical report accompanying the reform proposal, suggests that Albania is experiencing a growing concentration of its population in an ever-smaller number of urban centres, while the rest of the country is losing residents, functions and development capacity.

The index results show that only 13 municipalities are classified as having a high level of urban mass and are home to 62.5 per cent of the population.

By contrast, 30 municipalities – covering almost half of the country’s administrative map – are classified as having a low level of urban mass and account for just 14.2 per cent of the population.

Another 18 municipalities fall into the intermediate or medium category.

According to the data, the country’s population is concentrated in the capital, which is home to more than half a million people, followed at a considerable

distance by the municipalities of Durres, Vlora, Elbasan, Shkoder, Fieri, Kamza and Berat.

At the other end of the scale, municipalities such as Pustec, Libohova, Himara, Kelcyra, Memaliaj, Selenica, Dropull, Finiq, Delvina and Kolonja have the smallest populations.

The ruling-party experts did not build the index solely on population size. It also combines other indicators, including population density, the spatial distribution of residents, the demographic dependency ratio and the level of urbanisation.

This means that a municipality may cover a large area, but if its population is concentrated in a small town while the rest of its territory is largely empty, it is considered structurally weak.

One of the most significant findings is that, on average, 57 per cent of Albania’s territory is uninhabited.

The analytical document notes that the country no longer has the same population distribution it had in 2014, when the current administrative-territorial division was introduced with the aim of creating larger and more efficient municipalities.

“Some areas have grown, while others have lost a significant share of their population,” the report says, arguing that some municipalities are struggling to secure sustainable finances, qualified staff and adequate administrative capacity.

The Socialists have submitted a bill to parliament proposing a new administrative-territorial map that would merge several smaller municipalities with larger neighbouring ones – without explaining how the proposed map would address these underlying problems.

The proposal has faced opposition from residents in the affected areas. Some fear mergers will leave them with even more limited access to public services.

World.title: Kosovo Detains Man Suspected of Spying for Serbian Intelligence
World.content:
Fehim Sali, second left, at a court hearing in Pristina on August 14, 2026. Photo: BIRN

Pristina Basic Court on Friday ordered 30 days of detention for a dual Kosovo and Serbia citizen, Fehim Sali, who is suspected of spying for Serbia’s intelligence agency, the BIA.

It is alleged that he passed the BIA information about Kosovo officials, politicians and Islamist radicals, including potential recruitment targets, and received money in return.

Sali, a resident of Kosovo’s southern Dragash/Dragas municipality, was arrested on Thursday at the Merdare border crossing point while entering from Serbia. He appeared before the Basic Court in Pristina on Friday.

“The court’s assessment took into account the circumstances relating to the risk of absconding, the risk of influencing witnesses and evidence, and the risk of repetition or continuation of the criminal offence,” the court said in a statement.

According to the prosecution file, Sali is suspected of “maintaining contact with BIA officers using four different mobile phones”, which were found during raids at his house on Thursday, alongside around 40,000 euros in cash.

The prosecution file alleges that Sali “worked as a recruited agent for Serbia’s Security Information Agency, BIA, in exchange for material benefits”. The file alleges that he acted on the instructions of a senior BIA officer identified as Zelimir Matovic, nicknamed Zeljko.

It alleges that Sali provided the BIA with information about Kosovo’s political situation and helped it identify officials of Kosovo’s own intelligence agency, the AKI. According to the case file, he photographed some of its officials to facilitate their identification.

Sali is also accused of providing information about members of the radical Islamist Wahhabi movement as well as other people whom he allegedly proposed to the BIA officer as potential targets for contact and recruitment.

According to prosecutors, Sali also “mediated matters and documents connected to Serbian state institutions and maintained contacts with people with political and social influence in Serbia and Kosovo, particularly members of non-majority communities”.

The prosecution stated that he provided some of these people with “guidance on political activity, with the aim of gathering and transmitting information of interest to the BIA”.

Prosecutors argue that these activities were carried out against the state interests of Kosovo and endangered its constitutional order and national security.

The prosecution also alleges that the 40,000 euros found and seized during a search of Sali’s home came from his alleged activities on behalf of the BIA.

According to the case file, the evidence against Sali includes his own statement.

Prosecutors claim he described in detail his alleged activities, including how and where he communicated with BIA officials, exchanged information and provided assistance to the Serbian intelligence service.

Prosecutor Bekim Kodraliu told media that Sali admitted having been recruited and maintained regular contact with BIA officials.

“The suspect himself stated that he had been recruited and had ongoing contacts with BIA officials,” Kodraliu said.

The case comes two months after another Kosovo espionage conviction involving Serbia’s intelligence service.

In June, the Pristina Basic Court sentenced a Kosovo Albanian man, Hysri Selimi, a former Islamic State member, to six years in prison for espionage.

Prosecutors said Selimi had provided the BIA with information about religious radicalisation in Kosovo, former members of the Kosovo Liberation Army, KLA, and people who had joined Islamic State.

World.content:
Significant traffic changes are to affect Tallinn public transport, drivers and pedestrians this coming weekend as the city hosts the annual Ironman triathlon event.

The race will mean road closures, parking restrictions, and public transport diversions in place from Saturday, 22 August and Sunday, 23 August, as the full triathlon and the 70.3 variant go ahead.

The activities mostly affect Haabersti in the west, Põhja-Tallinn to the north and also areas to the south, as the swimming event is to be held on Lake Raku.

Bus route diversions will impact multiple services across both days. Routes 8, 21, 25, 26, 41, 42 and 54 will be diverted from Saturday morning until 8 p.m. on the Sunday. Routes 27, 36 and 61 will be diverted during daytime hours on both days, with a temporary route 77 operating between Oja tee and Harkujärve stops to the west of the city. Route 62 will be suspended entirely, while route 57 will face morning-only diversions.

Road closures include Viljandi mnt, which will be closed between Valdeku tänav and the Kangru junction from 5 a.m. to 12.15 p.m. on Saturday, and from 6.50 a.m. to 12.35 p.m. on Sunday. Paldiski mnt will be closed from Tuuleveski tänav to Tutermaa from 7.30 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Saturday, and from 8.35 a.m. to 4.35 p.m. on Sunday.

World.title: Wildlife expert: No large wild animal in Estonia seeks to attack humans
World.content:
Peep Männil, a wildlife expert at the Environmental Agency, says that estimating the numbers of large carnivores involves drones, trail cameras, tracking signs, observations and bioacoustics. No large wild animal in Estonia seeks out humans, he adds.

"It is possible to estimate the numbers of large carnivores, but directly counting the animals is not. Most of them are also nocturnal. The only large wild animal counted individually is the grey seal. This is possible because in spring and summer they gather for molting, and drones can count them one by one," explained Männil, senior specialist and wolf researcher at the Environmental Agency.

Monitoring methods for land‑dwelling wild animals rely on counting activity signs or selecting a specific group within the population — for example, females with offspring, who are fewer and easier to count, Männil noted.

Counts of large carnivores — wolves, lynxes, bears and jackals — are based on observations. "These are incidental observations," Männil added. "Hunters have been required for years to collect certain data. Monitoring is divided into two parts: hunters gather the initial data, and the Environmental Agency compiles and analyzes it."

Some areas may be left out of observations, Männil said. For example, no observations are conducted in protected areas.

The bear photographed in Saaremaa. Source: RMK

The Environmental Agency also collects its own data, especially concerning wolves. "Wolves have very high reproductive potential, and their numbers can change significantly within a year. We have quite a few trail cameras out and also use baiting for both wolves and jackals," Männil said. "Bioacoustics is the main method across Europe."

"For ungulates, we also conduct pellet counts, and hunters carry out winter tracking counts," he added.

"No large wild animal in Estonia seeks out humans. Large animals have a strong fear of humans, so it doesn't happen. In our nature, the creatures that 'seek' humans are small insects — horseflies, ticks and mosquitoes," Männil pointed out. "A mother bear may attack to protect her cubs, and then it's best to retreat. Usually these incidents happen because neither the human nor the bear notices the other until the distance is extremely small."

The highest‑risk period is early spring, when cubs are small and cannot yet follow their mother. "The same can happen with wild boars — a sow may attack if her piglets are in the nest," Männil said. "Generally, animals hear humans coming from far away and move off long before the person arrives."

World.title: Nurse shortage remains severe in Estonia despite higher enrollment
World.content:
Although interest in studying to become a nurse has increased, representatives of the Estonian Nurses Union say the country is still short at least 4,000 nurses. The need for specialist nurses is also steadily growing.

Admission numbers to the Tallinn Health University of Applied Sciences nursing program in recent years show strong interest in the profession. After the first round of admissions this year, there were 5.1 applications per nursing study place in the capital.

In Kohtla‑Järve, where the facility has a branch, competition was 3.7 applications per place, said Kristi Rannus, associate professor at the a health‑education institution's nursing department.

"So our problem right now is not a lack of interest in studying nursing. The question is rather how many we can train at once and how to make the best use of graduates' competencies in the health‑care system," she said.

Despite the high interest, Rannus said the need for nurses in health care remains large.

Tallinn Health University of Applied Sciences. Source: ERR

Estonian Nurses Union president Kätlin Lillemaa noted that Estonia currently has about 6.6 nurses per 1,000 residents, while the average in developed countries is around 9.2. To reach the OECD average, Estonia is short 4,000 nurses.

The need is also affected by the fact that, according to statistics, about 40 percent of nurses in Estonia are over 50 years old, and about 18 percent are older than 60, Lillemaa said.

"When we talk about a shortage of 4,000 nurses, then 40 percent of that would be needed to replace those retiring, 20 percent to cover workforce turnover, and the remaining 40 percent would be needed to increase the number of positions. In the past 10 years, nurses' independence and responsibilities have expanded significantly, and in recent years the number of people seeking help for mental‑health problems has grown sharply. With an aging population, chronic illnesses are more common, and nurses deal with many of these issues alongside doctors," Lillemaa explained.

Main entrance at Tartu University Hospital (TÜK). Source: Tartu University Hospital.

New colleagues are also constantly being sought at Tartu University Hospital, where nearly 1,800 nursing‑sector employees already work. Right now, nurses are needed in the surgical service, said Saima Hinno, member of the hospital's management board and head of nursing and patient experience.

"Health‑care institutions operate according to how they are funded by the state, what contracts they have and what volumes those contracts cover. We must also consider changes in the population, such as the broader provision of mental‑health services. When these opportunities open up for us, we must find colleagues who can provide those services," Hinno said.

Speakers also noted that alongside general nurses, the health‑care system increasingly needs specialist nurses.

"A specialist nurse's competence allows them to make independent decisions within their scope of practice. The decisions a nurse makes during a consultation are agreed upon within the care team. This trend is growing, so the need is there," Hinno said.

"I argue that once we have filled the workforce gaps, we should start thinking about a future‑proof health‑care system — meaning that not everyone does a little bit of everything, but each patient group is cared for by specialists with the appropriate training. Then we can begin improving the quality and accessibility of health‑care services," Rannus said.

World.title: Lego donation from Estonia helps Kenyan girls build science skills
World.content:
Dozens of kilograms of Lego bricks donated to an Estonian NGO are being eagerly embraced by girls in Kenya.

The donations aim to get more girls interested in science and engineering, and are already proving worthwhile.

Practical teaching aids and games are so costly in Kenya that they are beyond the means of many families, explained Emily Mirelle Vutt of NGO Mondo, which spearheaded the donation drive.

"Gender inequality is greater in Kenya," Vutt told Vikerraadio, noting "in Kenya, software developers and programmers tend to be men." Vutt lives for much of the year in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi.

Emily Mirelle Vutt. Source: Laura Raudnagel/ERR

"So we specifically targeted girls in order to give them more opportunities and increase their self-confidence, so that they too might see themselves working in science and technology one day."

The solution for NGO Mondo was to call on people to donate used Lego bricks of all shapes and sizes. These could even be used to teach robotics, for instance in Kisumu, a port city on Lake Victoria.

"We had a project where we provided robotics training to teachers in the rural Kisumu region of Kenya, who then run robotics clubs for children at schools," Vutt continued.

While often taken for granted as part of a European or American childhood, Legos are not as widespread in Kenya.

"It has been scientifically proven that Lego helps girls in particular take a step closer to science. The girls all did very well. Although they had never seen bricks like these before, they immediately started looking at how they could use them to build, for example, a motorcycle. Motorbikes are the main means of transport in Kenya," Vutt noted.

An assortment of lego bricks. Source: ERR

"One teacher told me that we had only seen robots in films, and now we can actually put them together with our own hands, and she was so happy. It was very nice to hear that," Vutt added.

Another issue in the country is that many children drop out of the school system, as they have to help out at home or to support their families, and do not have the money to go to school.

Vutt said when she first moved to Kenya, it took some getting used to. "But eventually you start to see the beauty in those differences," she added.

The tally of donated Lego bricks received by NGO Mondo was around 50 kilos all told, Vutt said. Since the average weight of a Lego brick is 1.67 grams, this figure would amount to around 30,000 bricks.

World.title: Estonian Refugee Council to expand operations in Gaza and West Bank
World.content:
The Estonian Refugee Council has established an official presence in the Palestinian territories to expand its humanitarian assistance and livelihoods programmes.

The new presence will allow ERC to expand its work in both Gaza and the West Bank, with a particular focus on cash-based humanitarian assistance and livelihoods recovery, it said in a statement.

"We have been working in the occupied Palestinian territory with local partners since autumn 2025. Establishing a permanent presence means that we can now remain engaged at a time when the need for humanitarian assistance has by no means disappeared with the ceasefire," said Eero Janson, director of the Estonian Refugee Council.

"In Gaza, a large share of the population continues to depend on humanitarian assistance, while displacement and protection needs are increasing across the West Bank. Being present locally will allow us to respond more quickly with our partners, reach people whose needs might otherwise remain unmet, and gradually complement emergency assistance with support for people to rebuild their livelihoods," he said.

The Estonian Refugee Council has been working with a local partner and with support from private donors in Estonia and the Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs to provide food assistance to hospitals across the territory since 2025.

More than 12,000 food parcels were handed out, helping to ensure daily meals for both patients and hospital staff working under extremely challenging conditions.

The agency provides immediate assistance in emergencies and supports crisis-affected people in rebuilding their lives.

The ERC is the largest humanitarian organisation in the Baltics and currently operates in Estonia, Ukraine, Armenia, Syria, Sudan and the occupied Palestinian territory.

World.title: Pärnu council ousts mayor, elects Isamaa's Siim Suursild
World.content:
The new ruling coalition of the Pärnu city council passed a vote of no confidence in Mayor Kristel Voltenberg at its Monday session, even though she announced at the start of the meeting that she would resign. The council elected Siim Suursild (Isamaa) as the new mayor.

Of the 39 council members, 23 supported the non-confidence motion.

Voltenberg told the council that although her time in office was short (253 days), it was filled with everything she was able to give to Pärnu and its residents. She said she wished for more dignified conduct and a dignified departure. She submitted her resignation and simultaneously an application to restore her mandate as a city council member.

Council chairman Andrei Korobeinik (Center Party) said that the last time a mayor faced a no‑confidence vote in Pärnu was more than 20 years ago.

At the same session, the council elected Siim Suursild as the new mayor. Under the coalition agreement, the mayor's position belongs to Isamaa, while the chair of the city council remains with the Center Party. The third partner in the coalition is EKRE.

World.title: Pictures: illustrator Eiko Ojala's first solo exhibition opens in Viljandi
World.content:
On 15 August, Eiko Ojala's exhibition "Meele märkused" ("Mind Notes") opened at the Rüki Gallery in Viljandi.

Illustrator and artist Eiko Ojala has created illustrations for publications such as National Geographic, Time, Le Monde, Politico, New Yorker, Washington Post and New York Times. His first solo exhibition brings into focus a lesser‑shown part of his work.

In the exhibition, Ojala's recognizable visual language moves beyond an illustrative function and concentrates on depicting the relationships between space, form and psychological states.

At the center of the series is a figure surrounded by geometric surfaces and forms that reference institutional or strictly defined interiors. Bodies sink, bend or are pressed against surfaces that simultaneously support and restrict their movement.

In the series presented at the exhibition, the emphasis shifts from narrative depiction to observing how built environments and surrounding spaces silently organize bodies, direct movement and shape a person's inner world through these invisible systems.

The curator is Lilian Hiob‑Küttis. "Meele märkused" will remain open at the Rüki Gallery until 26 September.

World.title: Local flavors shine along Estonian lake's 175-kilometer food festival route
World.content:
Visitors flocked to Estonia's Lake Peipus region this weekend as dozens of local joints and pop-up cafes served up area favorites and fish for the Peipus Food Street festival.

The 9th annual Peipus Food Street featured nearly 40 local and pop-up cafes across the lakeshore region, along with three workshops, including one on making beef ribs with wild mushrooms.

Local ingredients were a focus, with fresh fish including perch taking center stage on many menus.

"This festival is about showcasing the richness of the Lake Peipus region, and how people turn that bounty into food," said chief organizer Triinu Akkermann.

"That's our goal — to offer high-quality food to people across Estonia," she added.

The 9th Peipus Food Street festival was held in Eastern Estonia on August 15–16. 2026. Source: ERR

Perch is especially popular this time of year, said local chef Tauno Laasik, who served it fried, charred and in soup. "August is prime time for fresh, delicious perch," he added.

Visitors could also pick up traditional Peipus-area onion pies (sibulapirukad) and preserves. Pop-up cafe owner Anna said her team got up and got to work around 6 a.m. to keep up with demand.

"It takes time to get everything ready," Anna said Sunday. "Today's a little less busy than yesterday, but we're still doing pretty well. A batch sells out about every half-hour."

'August rolls' with local fish

One location also featured a new dish this year. Vietnamese-born cook Trang said their cafe's spring rolls, redubbed "August rolls" for the occasion, have been a hit.

The 9th Peipus Food Street festival was held in Eastern Estonia on August 15–16. 2026. Source: ERR

"Everybody came back and told me, 'Oh, the sauce is so good, the fish is so fresh!'" Trang said.

Food lovers of all ages came from across Estonia and beyond for the occasion. Tartu County resident Krista said her group sampled several dishes, including perch, a stew, the spring rolls and dessert.

Another family from Pärnu County said they had visited five locations on Saturday and were making the most of Sunday before they had to hit the road back home.

Each diner had their own favorites, from fish and mushrooms to dainty desserts.

World.title: Coventry sign Nigeria striker Awoniyi from Forest
World.content:
London – Coventry signed Nigeria striker Taiwo Awoniyi from Nottingham Forest in a deal worth a reported £9 million ($12 million) on Monday.

Awoniyi will link up with Frank Lampard’s side in time for their opening game of the Premier League season at champions Arsenal on Friday.

He is Lampard’s latest recruit following the signings of Gus Hamer, Carl Rushworth, Loum Tchaouna, Aurele Amenda and Caleb Yirenkyi.

Coventry are back in the Premier League for the first time in 25 years after winning the Championship last season.

“I am very excited about this season, and I can’t wait to get started,” Awoniyi said.

“I’m really looking forward to working with my new teammates. I have seen how amazing they have been last season, coming up from the Championship.

“They were incredible and now I am just excited to join them.”

Awoniyi, capped 10 times by Nigeria, said farewell to the City Ground when he was given a guard of honour by the Forest squad during their pre-season friendly against Brest on Sunday.

The 29-year-old spent four seasons at Forest, scoring 23 goals in 103 games in all competitions before losing his place for much of last term.

He was placed in an induced coma in May 2025 after rupturing an intestine when he collided with a post during a game against Leicester.

“Taiwo will always have a special place in the history of Nottingham Forest,” the club’s owner Evangelos Marinakis said.

“He has been one of the defining figures in our journey and given our supporters moments of great joy that will never be forgotten.”

World.title: US-Palestinian says ‘terrified’ as he returns to property besieged by settlers
World.content:
Tel Aviv – The Palestinian-American owner of a house besieged by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank said on Monday he feared for his safety as he headed back to his property and called for US protection.

Louai Abu Ridi owns one of the three houses in Qusra, near Nablus, which settlers began besieging more than a week ago, trapping residents inside and effectively blocking supplies, generating condemnation around the world.

His brother, Qusai Abu Ridi, is stuck inside the house and has been relaying the situation of residents to the outside world.

On Monday, the brother shared videos with AFP showing settlers riding quad bikes past the house while Israeli forces were stationed outside.

“I’ve been watching this live for many days and now this is the second week I can’t sleep,” Louai Abu Ridi told reporters after he landed at Israel’s Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv.

“I can’t let the settlers steal my house while I was watching,” he added.

Abu Ridi said he was hoping to stay in the house on Monday night, which left him “terrified”.

“I’m asking the US officials, the embassy, to provide me protection,” he said.

“I was terrified for my brother and his son. Fearing for his safety. Now I’m going to fear for my own safety. And I’m not sure how the struggle is going to be for me to get there. And if I get there, are they going to allow me to go in and out freely in my own house? I’ll find out today.”

Abu Ridi voiced frustration at the Israeli military’s inability to remove a handful of settlers from the site and called for more action to resolve the situation.

“It’s time for everyone to act. I heard a saying in America, talk the talk and walk the walk. So if they’re talking on social media and they condemn it, so they need an action on the ground,” he said.

The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, a staunch supporter of settlers, has offered unusually strong criticism over the incident in recent days.

“Actions by those who carried out this horrific act of terror meant to intimidate and harass this family are disgusting,” Huckabee wrote on X on Thursday.

World.title: Iraq’s oil pipeline to Syria’s Baniyas to take four years to complete
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Sources told Reuters that the oil pipeline Iraq plans to construct to the Syrian port of Baniyas will take four years to complete at a cost of at least $15 billion.

The initiative, supported by a partnership including US-based Chevron, aims to minimize dependency on the Strait of Hormuz, which has been closed due to the conflict between Iran and the United States.

US Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent stated last week that prior to the conflict, a fifth of the world’s oil and gas supplies were transported through the Strait of Hormuz. However, he noted that between 50 and 70 percent of those exports will flow via underground pipelines instead.

The Kirkuk-Baniyas oil pipeline is being revived to export one million barrels of Iraqi oil per day.

The initiative represents a genuine opportunity arising from the present maritime difficulties facing ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Steps have already been taken to revive the ancient 800-kilometer Kirkuk-Baniyas oil pipeline, which was built in 1952 and had previously been destroyed because of instability.

The project is anticipated to boost energy ties between the two countries and attract foreign investment.

Syria’s Deputy Energy Minister for Oil Affairs, Ghiath Diab, said that pumping stations along the pipeline are mostly destroyed and need extensive repairs.

The repairs include upgrading pipes, storage tanks, pumps, electrical systems, and civil engineering, according to Diab.

Renovating the old line while creating a new one will increase the project’s economic feasibility, according to the Syrian official.

Damascus and Baghdad are advancing efforts to rehabilitate the pipeline, which aims to give Iraq direct access to European markets via the Mediterranean.

World.title: Iraqi finance minister meets Princess Astrid of Liechtenstein
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Finance Faleh Sari emphasized on Monday the increasing interest of investors in the opportunities present in Iraq.

Sari’s remarks took place during his meeting with Princess Astrid of Liechtenstein, where the discussions focused on economic relations and opportunities for cooperation between Iraq and Liechtenstein, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Ministry of Finance.

Sari highlighted the importance of expanding communications with international partners to attract investments that support development and help diversify the Iraqi economy.

The finance minister stated that Iraq offers promising opportunities in different economic areas. He added that the next phase would involve leveraging foreign experience and finance to strengthen the productive and service sectors.

Princess Astrid expressed interest in the opportunities present in Iraq, emphasizing the importance of maintaining connections with key Iraqi organizations to identify areas for collaboration in the upcoming term.

The meeting follows Sari’s confirmation that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has had a direct impact on his country’s economy, citing the relationship between trade, oil flows, and developments in the region.

The Iraqi Ministry of Finance is committed to tackling the current situation by increasing non-oil revenue, developing financial management tools, and advancing the reform process, according to Sari.

Sari indicated earlier that the Iraqi government is moving forward with the establishment of its first performance-based budget in history, which relies on a new approach to manage public expenditure.

World.title: Pentagon inks Tomahawk deal amid reports of missile shortfall
World.content:
Washington – The Pentagon announced a $22.9 billion contract with Raytheon on Monday for Tomahawk missiles amid reports of a shortfall due to the war with Iran.

Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao said the contract will “accelerate Tomahawk missile delivery to our warfighters at unprecedented speed.”

“Guaranteeing our naval and joint forces have the lethal firepower they need to deter aggression and protect the homeland is paramount,” Cao said in a statement. “The Department is utilizing every available tool to meet the demands of our current operations.”

An analysis by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) think tank released last month found that US stocks of Patriot and THAAD air defense missiles have been slashed by the conflict with Iran.

Before it began in late February, the United States had more than 2,300 Patriot and more than 450 THAAD interceptors — figures that CSIS estimated have been roughly halved or more in the subsequent months of war.

The Washington Post reported this month that President Donald Trump had demanded answers from Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth about munitions shortages at a recent cabinet meeting.

Trump and Hegseth both later denied that the United States was faced with dwindling missile stocks.

Tomahawk missiles are mainly launched from submarines and warships and can travel more than 1,600 kilometers (1,000 miles).

World.title: Economist: Dinar redenomination traps corrupt cash but faces obstacles
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Prominent Iraqi economic expert Ziyad Al-Hashemi stated on Monday, August 17, 2026, that the proposed plan to replace the national currency and remove three zeros from the Iraqi Dinar will systematically “legitimize clean dinars and invalidate dirty dinars.”

Al-Hashemi argued that replacing banknotes restricts illicit money circulation, blocks back-door laundering through real estate and gold, and confines circulating currency to formal state-supervised channels. However, he cautioned that entrenched political and financial figures holding massive volumes of hoarded corrupt cash will likely orchestrate multi-front political resistance to obstruct implementation.

Economic Analysis & Structural Debate

Isolating Illicit Capital: Replacing legacy banknotes will strip illicit actors of the ability to inject hoarded dinars into the market, as legacy currency not submitted to banking compliance checks will permanently lose legal tender status.

Limited Laundering Avenues: Attempts to launder hoarded cash through luxury real estate, gold bullion, or parallel U.S. dollars during the transitional window will face severe friction due to financial auditing compliance, anti-money laundering (AML) controls, and physical supply constraints.

The 8 Trillion IQD Money Contraction: Reaffirms statements by Telecom Minister Mustafa Sanad regarding an estimated 8 trillion IQD ($6.1 billion) in unexchanged cash that could permanently exit circulation if unverified funds cannot pass source-of-wealth scrutiny.

Implementation Obstacles: Al-Hashemi warned that influential figures implicated in large-scale corruption schemes will leverage administrative pretexts and political resistance to stall or derail the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) execution plans.

Skepticism Over Root Causes: Competing economic analysts argue that redenomination serves as “cosmetic economic makeup” addressing liquidity symptoms rather than core structural illicit flows, pointing out that major embezzled fortunes have already transitioned into foreign offshore holdings, external bank accounts, and international real estate beyond the reach of domestic currency reforms.

The debate underscores the complex operational stakes surrounding Iraq’s monetary restructuring plans.

While advocates see redenomination as a powerful tool to enforce banking compliance, flush out cash hoards, and contract the monetary base, its ultimate effectiveness hinges on the Central Bank of Iraq’s ability to maintain strict exchange limits, enforce transparency audits, and resist institutional pushback.

World.title: Iran Central Bank Chief in Baghdad to recover $11B and expand $12B trade
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Governor of the Central Bank of Iran (CBI), Abdolnaser Hemmati, arrived in Baghdad leading a high-level economic delegation on an official visit to negotiate the recovery of approximately $11 billion in Iranian funds and receivables held in Iraq and strengthen cross-border trade flows.

According to reports published by official state channels, Hemmati’s schedule includes bilateral sessions on Monday, August 17, 2026, with Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) Governor Nizar Nasir Hussein, the Iraqi Minister of Finance, and Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi.

Key Discussion Pillars & Financial Metrics

Recovering $11B in Frozen Assets:Unlocking mechanisms to settle outstanding gas and electricity export arrears, comprising roughly $7 billion deposited at the Central Bank of Iraq and over $3 billion in dues owed to Iran’s Ministry of Petroleum.

Pre-War Trade Benchmarks:Hemmati noted that Iranian non-oil exports to Iraq stood at approximately $12 billion prior to recent regional military escalations, emphasizing Tehran’s commitment to protecting and expanding private-sector commercial volumes.

Joint Economic Committee:Finalizing arrangements with Iraqi Minister of Trade to convene the upcoming Iran–Iraq Joint Economic Commission in Baghdad, co-chaired on the Iranian side by the Minister of Economic Affairs and Finance.

Investor & Contractor Grievances:Hemmati held consultative sessions in Baghdad with Iranian contractors, traders, and private investors operating in Iraq, agreeing to escalate issues concerning currency repatriations, customs tariffs, and project payments directly to Prime Minister Al-Zaidi.

Hemmati’s mission builds on high-level talks held during Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s July visit to Tehran, focusing on humanitarian clearing mechanisms, goods-for-debt settlements, and trade escrow accounts.

By establishing alternative commercial clearing arrangements, Tehran seeks to secure essential commodity imports and safeguard cross-border commerce while navigating international banking constraints and liquidity pressures.

World.title: Drone assault hits office of Iraqi Kurdistan’s prime minister
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Two explosive-laden drones launched from Iranian territory targeted on Monday Iraqi Kurdistan Prime Minister Masrour Barzani’s private office and the home of a top intelligence official.

According to official briefings from the Kurdistan Region Counter-Terrorism Directorate, the precise attacks resulted in no casualties or injuries.

The attack’s major targets were Prime Minister Masrour Barzani’s private office and the house of the director of the Parastin Security and Intelligence Agency, according to Reuters.

The strikes took place in Erbil province’s Pirmam area, which is around 30 kilometers north of the capital.

Security personnel recognized the drone as an Iranian-designed “Hadid-110” kamikaze drone carrying explosive payloads.

Barzani condemned the attack in a statement on X (formerly Twitter), describing it as illegitimate and unacceptable. He also cautioned that the strike was a dangerous escalation that posed a direct threat to Iraqi Kurdistan’s security and stability.

While Tehran and Iran-backed armed groups have previously accused Iraqi Kurdistan of hosting hostile Iranian Kurdish opposition groups, the authorities in the Kurdistan region of Iraq have always denied using their territory to threaten neighboring nations.

The incident represents a serious escalation of the region’s ongoing cross-border drone and missile strikes on essential infrastructure and residential areas.

World.title: From 5,921m summit, historic glide to Ladakh roadhead
World.content:
JAMMU/LEH: From a towering 5,921-metre summit, two Indian mountaineers made history by paragliding directly to a roadhead in Ladakh, combining a high-altitude ascent with a pioneering aerial descent, the Army said Monday.

Colonel Hem Chandra Singh, principal of Jawahar Institute of Mountaineering & Winter Sports (JIM & WS), and mountaineer Manish Makholia launched their paragliders from the summit of Mt Delta-41, also known as Mt Barmal, in Tangol region of Kargil, and landed safely at the Road Head Camp in Tangol village, around 3,600 metres, an Army spokesperson said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

After acclimatisation, the 13-member JIM & WS expedition, led by Col Singh, established base camp and split into two groups amid adverse weather and a limited window.

One team reached the 5,921-metre peak amid sub-zero temperatures on Independence Day. The second team reached the summit at 6.10am on Aug 16 after setting out at 3am, the spokesperson said.

The team comprised Col Hem Chandra Singh (team leader), Capt Anupam Singh (medical officer), Mahfooz Ilahi Hajam (team manager), Hony Capt/Sub Maj Rafiq Ahmad Malik (Retd), Manish Makholia, and nine others from various parts of the country.

Officials said this was the first-ever paragliding descent from the summit directly to base, a feat âunprecedented in Indian adventure sports historyâ.

World.title: 'Follow law of land': Centre to X after Musk announces greater visibility on govt censorship
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Centre on Monday said that Elon Musk-owned X will have to "follow the law of the land" after the social media platform introduced a new rule to make government-driven restrictions on content more visible to users.

"X will have to follow the law of the land," the officer told news agency PTI.

In a post on social media platform X, Musk said that any censorship required by governments is now clearly visible, signalling the platform's intention to provide users with greater insight into actions taken at the request of government authorities.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"Any censorship required by governments is now clearly visible," Musk said.

Under the proposed changes, X users will be able to see when governments seek the removal of posts or request restrictions on accounts.

The platform also plans to disclose details about the agencies making such requests and, where available, the legal grounds or justification cited for the action.

The move is part of Musk's wider push to make the platform's moderation and content-distribution systems more transparent.

Since acquiring X, formerly known as Twitter, Musk has repeatedly argued that users should have greater visibility into how online content is moderated and ranked.

World.title: 'Intentionally didn't take action': Himanta on Chidambaram's 'dimagi naxal' remark
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Assam chief minister

on Monday launched a sharp attack against former Union home minister

for claiming to be a "dimagi naxal" after Prime Minister

's remark, asking for a probe into whether he intentionally did not take any action against Naxalism during his tenure.

In a press conference, Sarma said, "There should be a probe against Chidambaram who claims to be a "dimagi Naxal". Was he intentionally not taking any action against Naxalism during his tenure?"

This comes after Chidambaram took a swipe at PM Modi's Independence Day speech and said, "I am proud to be a dimagi naxal!"

Earlier on Saturday, PM Modi, during his Independence Day speech, said that while Naxals who took up arms in the jungle have been eliminated, there are also "dimagi naxals" in various parts of the country who need to be "identified and isolated."

"For years, people with Maoist thinking were there in public life. Even in government committees, this thinking had affected various institutions and initiatives. My dear countrymen, we have been able to curb and free the country from 'hathariya naxal' (armed naxal)," the Prime Minister said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"Even if these naxals are gone, the 'dimagi naxal' (people with naxal thinking) are looking for an opportunity, looking to see ways of violence, and trying to drag the country to a wrong path.





We need to identify these dimagi naxal, isolate them, and bring the youth together for a developed country," he added.

The opposition latched on to PM Modi's remarks and dismissed them as hollow political rhetoric.

Senior Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said that the term carries no real substance, drawing a parallel with previous debates surrounding the phrase "urban naxal".

"Two or three years ago, he (PM Modi) called his political opponents 'urban naxals'. At that time, the question arose in Parliament as to what the definition of 'Urban Naxal' was. The home minister replied that there is no such thing as an 'urban naxal', nor is there any definition for it. Today, the Prime Minister is using the term 'mental naxal' (ideological Naxal) for his political opponents from the Red Fort," Jairam Ramesh alleged.

World.title: 253 held across 14 states as security forces bust ISI-backed terror network
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a major crackdown on terror ahead of Independence Day, security agencies have busted the ISI-backed Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN) active in the country, arresting 253 operatives in over 80 FIRs registered across 14 states and thwarting the networkâs plans to carry out subversive attacks around August 15.

Pakistani-based gangster-terrorist Shahzad Bhatti, who is popular on social media, runs a network that scouts online for "vulnerable" Muslim youths across India who may belong to low-income groups, are 'disgruntled' or engaging in drug abuse; radicalises them; and thereafter gives them tasks like espionage, reconnaissance of potential targets, collect and transport arms sent via drones from Pakistan and engage in attacks through use of firearms and grenades.

The 253 persons arrested in coordinated operations across multiple locations in 14 states, are Indian youths recruited by SBN to foment trouble around in their own country.

To counter SBN-linked disruptions planned around Independence Day, a coordinated multi-state operation was carried out on August 12 using a real-time intelligence-sharing system with state police forces. Of the 253 detentions made across 14 states, 62 were in Uttar Pradesh; 52 in Haryana; 51 in Delhi; 44 in Punjab; 15 in Rajasthan; 8 in Maharashtra; 5 in Uttarakhand; three each in Karnataka, Gujarat and Bihar; and two each in Telangana, Himachal Pradesh, J&K and Kerala â with fresh FIRs registered in Delhi and Karnataka.





Home minister Amit Shah posted on X on Monday: "Modi govt destroyed the ISI-backed terror group Shahzad Bhatti Network ahead of Independence Day and thwarted its plans for subversive attacks by arresting more than 200 operatives. Indian security forces ripped apart the network by launching coordinated operations across different locations in 14 states, upholding (a) brilliant example of India's zero-tolerance towards terrorism".

Shah added that the substantial recoveries made from the operatives of the ISI-funded group and their hideouts include IEDs, grenades bearing Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings, pistols, live cartridges and CCTV cameras used for espionage. "The network was involved in several terrorist activities," he shared.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

MHA in a statement said that SBN is a Pakistani-based, ISI-backed syndicate linked to grenade, IED and petrol bomb attacks and targeted killings across India.

It has also been paying local conduits to recce police, defence and religious sites, and to install CCTV cameras for espionage, added the ministry.

Cumulatively, over 80 FIRs and 200-plus arrests have been recorded against SBN under UAPA, BNS, the Arms Act, NDPS Act and Explosive Substances Act. Recovery of grenades bearing Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings confirm the networkâs direct cross-border links.

"Security agencies reaffirm govt of Indiaâs zero tolerance for cross-border terror and continued coordinated action to dismantle SBNâs networks nationwide," said the home ministry.

World.title: Nitin's 'Nabin' team: BJP hits reset button with eye on Uttar Pradesh and 'Mission 2029'

World.title: 326 MPs, 14 CMs, over 4,000 cases: Report lays bare criminalisation of politics before SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A fresh status report submitted to the Supreme Court has highlighted criminal cases against elected representatives, with 326 sitting MPs and chief ministers of 14 states having declared cases against them.

The report, filed by senior advocate Vijay Hansaria, the amicus curiae assisting the court in a PIL seeking speedy disposal of criminal cases against MPs and MLAs, said 251 of the 543 Lok Sabha members and 75 of the 233 Rajya Sabha members have criminal cases pending against them.

The figures are based on data from the Association for Democratic Reforms. Among Lok Sabha MPs facing cases, 170 have declared serious criminal cases carrying a possible sentence of five years or more.

In the Rajya Sabha, 40 of the 75 MPs facing cases have serious charges.

The report also puts the number of criminal cases pending against current and former MPs and MLAs at 4,192. Hansaria noted that despite the Supreme Court and high courts monitoring these matters for faster trials, the overall pendency has remained largely unchanged since 2018.

Data compiled from various high courts showed that 1,243 cases were disposed of in 2025, while 1,050 new cases were registered during the same year.





14 chief ministers have criminal cases

The affidavit said 14 of the country's 28 chief ministers have declared criminal cases, including serious offences.

Telangana CM Revanth Reddy has the highest number among the chief ministers listed, with 89 cases, followed by West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari with 29 and Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar with 19.

Kerala MPs top state-wise list

The state-wise analysis showed particularly high proportions of MPs with declared criminal cases in several states.

Kerala topped the list, with 19 of its 20 MPs facing criminal charges, including 11 with serious cases. Telangana followed, with 14 of 17 MPs facing criminal charges.

In Odisha, 16 of 21 MPs, or 76%, have criminal cases, while Jharkhand has 10 of its 14 MPs facing charges. Tamil Nadu recorded 26 of its 39 MPs with criminal cases.

Around half of the MPs from several other major states, including Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, West Bengal, Bihar, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, have criminal cases.

The numbers were significantly lower in some states. Haryana and Chhattisgarh had one MP each facing criminal charges, while Punjab had two of 13. Assam had three of 14 MPs, Delhi three of seven, Rajasthan four of 25, Gujarat five of 25 and Madhya Pradesh nine of 29.

The analysis did not include Uttar Pradesh because the Allahabad High Court had not submitted its report.

Amicus seeks dedicated courts, one-year deadline

Hansaria has urged SC to strengthen the mechanism for monitoring criminal cases involving lawmakers and ensure that they are concluded within a fixed timeframe.

He has proposed that courts designated as special courts for MPs and MLAs should exclusively hear trials involving lawmakers until those matters are completed, instead of being assigned other regular judicial work.

Hansaria is assisting the court in a PIL filed by BJP leader Ashwini Upadhyay seeking expeditious disposal of criminal cases against lawmakers.

SC had, in a November 9, 2023 judgment, issued directions aimed at accelerating the disposal of thousands of criminal cases involving MPs and MLAs. It had asked high courts to constitute special benches to monitor the progress of such cases and directed special courts to avoid adjournments except for "rare and compelling reasons".

The court had also directed that criminal cases against members of Parliament, legislative assemblies and legislative councils be given priority.

, with 10 women and six leaders from minority communities finding a place among the national office-bearers.

Former Union minister

World.title: Opium farmers demand more farming licences, ₹1 lakh per kg
World.content:
Ahead of the announcement of the opium licensing policy for 2026-27, scheduled for September, opium farmers from Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh have urged the Union Government to formulate it in a manner that benefits the country and farmers.

At a protest meeting in Jantar Mantar here on Monday (August 17, 2026), under the banner of Bharatiya Afeem Kisan Sangharsh Samiti, the licensee farmers said the number of opium licenses for medicinal opium cultivation should be increased, and the price of opium procured by the Government should be hiked to ₹1,00,000 per kg for farmers, in line with the international market price.

The farmers said in a representation to the Government that the opium leases that have been cancelled since 1990 should be reinstated, so that the cultivation of opium, which has increased significantly since 2008, can be further expanded. “Morphine content depends on natural factors and is not in the farmers’ control. Therefore, opium leases should be granted based on a morphine yield of three kgs per hectare,” they demanded.

The farmers said the poppy straws should be excluded from the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act and claimed that they are not a narcotic substance but rather the husk of the poppy plant. The farmers demanded that the Concentrate of Poppy Straw (CPS) method of opium harvest, which the Government has been promoting based on international experience since the 2021-22 crop year, should be completely abolished, and the traditional opium cultivation should be promoted. “The government should rather purchase poppy straws at a rate of ₹2,000 per kg and process them for upgrading their quality,” they added.

As per the 2025-26 policy, nearly 1.21 lakh farmers are estimated to be eligible for licenses to cultivate opium in these States. “This represents a 23.5% increase over the number of licenses actually issued in the previous crop year. The policy thus brings approximately 15,000 additional farmers into the fold, who are expected to benefit from opium cultivation this year,” the Government had said in September, 2025 while announcing the new policy.

“The Central Government continues to ensure adequate supply of alkaloids to meet medical and palliative care needs. Concurrently, efforts are underway to augment processing capacity through indigenous and self-reliant measures, with a view to meeting the requirements of alkaloids for the production of essential narcotic drugs,” it added.

World.title: No State can block traditional routes of elephants: Supreme Court
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Monday (August 17, 2026) directed the Centre to conduct a nationwide survey and take steps to ensure the free passage of wild elephant herds through their ancient corridors across States without human will or habitations blocking or impeding their natural routes.

“No State can block their [elephants] paths. Blockading elephant corridors is not the solution to human-animal conflicts. Elephants travel across many States. One State cannot come in their way and block their traditional pathways. The solutions to this (animal-human conflict) are altogether different, and not constructing blockades,” Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said.

Justice Joymalya Bagchi, on the three-judge Bench with Justice V. Mohana, said elephant pathways were not State-specific, and herds travel far by nature.

“Elephant corridors have been obstructed, impeded, blocked due to some local factors. The Union of India must conduct a fresh survey and file a comprehensive report, which would include the necessary steps which were taken to prevent such obstructions,” Chief Justice Kant ordered.

The court directed the government to examine allegations that fireballs, mashaals (fire-torches) and spikes are thrown at wild elephants. In 2018, the apex court had prohibited the use of fireballs, burning rods, and spikes to chase elephants, calling them barbaric and illegal.

The court asked the government to ensure the implementation of the ban of such measures by ‘hula’ parties to drive away wild elephants from crops and villages. Elephants are Schedule I animals under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. They are considered a vulnerable species which receive absolute legal protection.

Appearing for the Centre, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati agreed to conduct a nationwide survey and submit the status report. Ms. Bhati sought three months, but the court said it would list the case after eight weeks to check on progress.

“Construction of any kind of obstacle or creating blockades in elephant corridors is not acceptable. We are very clear that there cannot be obstacles in the way of wildlife. No State can say that just because crops are getting destroyed, they will have to construct obstacles on their path,” the Bench reiterated.

Justice Bagchi said the practice of using fireballs and spikes was prevalent in West Bengal where the elephants came from Nepal and went to Jharkhand and other States. Chief Justice Kant said there were elephants in the Yamuna Nagar area of Haryana which travel to Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh.

The court was hearing a plea by advocate Shibani Ghosh, who submitted that fireballs continue to be thrown at wild elephants in West Bengal to drive them away from human habitation and croplands despite Supreme Court orders in 2018 to desist from the practice.

World.title: Bigger profile comes with a formidable challenge for Deepak Mhaskey
World.content:
Deepak Mhaskey — whose name was announced as the Bharatiya Janata Party’s new national social media convener on Monday (August 17, 2026) — is seen as a strong backroom figure in his home State of Chhattisgarh. However, taking up a bigger role at a time when the party is being forced back to the drawing board to connect with the youth, the spotlight is expected to be firmly on him and his team.

Soon after Mr. Mhaskey’s name was announced, the 58-year-old Chemistry professor-turned-politician was asked how he would engage with the youth, to which he replied that it would be through “reels” and that they [the youth] were already on social media and the party would try to reach them through the same.

The reply was in his own mild-mannered style, one that has drawn comparisons with his long-serving predecessor Amit Malviya, who was known to be more aggressive. Mr. Mhaskey, who has served as a State-level spokesperson and had headed the State social media cell in the past, was known as someone who was not very regular on TV debates and one who presented the party’s point of view on local media steadily but calmly.

Anti-graft campaign

Those who have worked with him, however, say that he may come across as unassuming but can shift gears when needed. A case in point, they say, was the party’s constant attack on the Bhupesh Baghel-led Congress government on the issue of corruption in the run-up to the 2023 Assembly polls by bombarding the popular social media networks with relevant posts and pictures. It was also the same period when the party’s current national president, Nitin Nabin, was the BJP in-charge of Chhattisgarh and had the opportunity to see Mr. Mhaskey’s work up close. Later, he also contributed to State election wins in West Bengal and Bihar, putting in use his data analysis skills, said party leaders.

Mr. Mhaskey was born into a Maharashtrian Brahmin family which has past connections with the BJP, including the erstwhile Jan Sangh, and the RSS. A profile shared by the party revealed that early in his career, he worked as a college chemistry professor for a few years.

“He is an avid agriculturist with over 35 years of experience in agricultural crops and organic farming. He is interested in data collection, analysis, and governance roles,” it added.

Mr. Mhaskey will be leading a team which will have Priti Gandhi, Alok Bhatt, Shiwanand Dwivedi and Arun Yadav.

While Mr. Mhaskey spoke of busting propaganda after the appointment, the BJP that has been ruling the country for over 12 years is facing questions on governance from a generation that is thinking, acting and connecting differently than the earlier ones. Party colleagues say that of his over three and a half decades, he has been dealing with social media for over 12 years and that makes him suitable for the role. Even Mr. Malviya, when he first took over as the social media chief had lesser experience as a BJP member, they say, even as they underline the need for a more balanced approach in current times.

Mr. Mhaskey was congratulated by Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai, other Chhattisgarh leaders, and Mr. Malviya. In a long post on X in which he congratulated the new office-bearers whose names were announced in Monday’s organisational reshuffle, Mr. Malviya wrote: “I wish to particularly congratulate Shri Deepak Mhaskey ji, who will be taking over from me as the head of the BJP’s Social Media Department...” making a specific mention of his successor.

World.title: Indian sailors’ SOS: ‘Company asking us to risk lives, cross Strait of Hormuz’
World.content:
Indian sailors aboard a ship in the Persian Gulf have sent out an SOS video alleging that their employer is telling them to transit the Strait of Hormuz despite the security risks and put their lives in danger. The SOS video was sent on a day reports said that Iran is ready to escalate tensions in the chokepoint as talks with the U.S. to end the conflict have stalled.

In a video posted on X by the Forward Seamen’s Union of India (FSUI), the master of AM Pioneer, a Marshall Islands-flagged vessel, Anil Raj said that the ship went to Ras Al Khaimah Port in the UAE last month for a survey.

“The company told us that we have to cross the Hormuz Strait to India when the (Strait of) Hormuz is open for the entire ships and it is very safe to navigate. Now, from last week, the company is forcing us to cross through Hormuz and go to Fujairah,” said Mr. Raj.

The ship’s master said that the “company is putting the blame on me, saying that I am misguiding the crew officers of this vessel against the company.”

The video then pans to show the crew standing behind Mr. Raj, who said that the company “tried to arrange one security and requested the Americans to give us air support to pass through Hormuz.”

The ship’s master said that “the company is trying to push us through Hormuz in a crooked way and put our lives in danger.”

The ship’s second engineer, who did not identify himself, appears in the video saying, “When Hormuz opens for all the ships that time, I can agree to pass.”

Another crew member added that when they joined the company, “they told us to keep the vessel ready and sail only when Hormuz is ready (safe).”

“But now we are being forced. We want our life safe and we will not cross Hormuz till it is safe (to do so),” he said.

Forcing Seafarers to strait of Death #Shipowners and managers of Marshall Islands-flagged vessel AM Pioneer are pressuring the Master to force its 16 Indian crew to transit the high-risk Strait of Hormuz.

The crew has clearly refused. They will not put their lives in danger. They… pic.twitter.com/AE1qfq1Byf — FSUI (@FSUIINDIA) August 17, 2026

According to ship-monitoring website Equasis, AM Pioneer is managed by Alphard Maritime Private Limited, a Mumbai-based company. It is an offshore supply vessel that transports equipment, crew, and essential supplies to offshore oil and gas platforms.

In its post on X, FSUI said that the shipowners and managers of AM Pioneer are “pressuring the Master to force its 16 Indian crew to transit the high-risk Strait of Hormuz”.

“The crew has clearly refused. They will not put their lives in danger. They will not sail under dark conditions with communications switched off. No seafarer should risk death for owners’ profits or convenience,” the association said.

World.title: Death of a Trinamool leader and corruption taint in Bengal politics
World.content:
On Sunday morning, the body of five-time Trinamool Congress MLA and former West Bengal Minister Ashish Banerjee was recovered from a party office next to his residence in Rampurhat in West Bengal’s Birbhum district. A purported note was recovered near the body in which he vehemently denied involvement in any kind of corruption.

Ashish, who taught at Rampurhat Government College before entering politics, was among the most humble and soft-spoken Trinamool Congress leaders. He served as the Deputy Speaker of the Assembly from 2021 to 2026, during the third and final term of the Mamata Banerjee government. His death has sent shock waves through the State. Leaders across parties, including those from the BJP, have described him as an honest politician and asserted that there could be no graft allegations against him.

To many, the 74-year-old leader from Birbhum was an exception, especially given that the district — known as a transit route for cattle and sand smuggling and home to a large number of stone quarries — has emerged as a hub of corruption. However, his clean image did little to protect Ashish from the political fallout after the regime change in Bengal.

Since the announcement of the Assembly poll results on May 4, the Trinamool Congress’s rank and file has been battling allegations of corruption. Slogans of ‘chor chor (thief thief)’ have also been directed at Ms. Banerjee, the party chairperson and former Chief Minister.

Scores of Trinamool leaders arrested on charges of extortion have been subjected to humiliation and mob violence while being produced in courts or taken into custody.

In some cases, the courts have asked the police to ensure that those in custody do not face such ordeals. In others, the courts have denied any relief. Earlier this month, when party MP Mahua Moitra approached the Supreme Court against a Calcutta High Court order asking her to appear in person in a case, the top court remarked, “Freedom fighters faced bullets, and you fear eggs?”

Rush to wash off taint

One reason that the Trinamool Congress split, with the majority of its leaders parting ways with Ms. Banerjee, was the desire to wash off the taint of corruption associated with the previous dispensation.

Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly Ritabrata Banerjee, who met the family members of the former Deputy Speaker, said many leaders are being made to take responsibility for the “mafia syndicate of the organised loot and legalised plunder” under the previous regime.

Loyalists of the former CM have highlighted Ashish’s death to claim that switching political allegiance does not guarantee protection from the ruling establishment. Opposition leaders in West Bengal have often referred to the “washing machine” that can “wash off” any graft allegations, provided one joins the BJP.

The Suvendu Adhikari government has been aggressively pursuing cases of wrongdoing under the previous regime.

While the Trinamool Congress has faced widespread criticism over corruption, the ruling establishment could resist the temptation to subject the accused to mob justice.

Politics is largely a matter of perception. It may take years before the cases of alleged corruption against Trinamool Congress leaders reach their legal conclusion. In the meanwhile, the allegations themselves can give licence to some to rail against “thieves” and deprive them of all goodwill.

Ashish’s death brings into focus the stress that Opposition party leaders are under, irrespective of whether they are with Ms. Banerjee or waiting to jump ship. Holding the guilty accountable is best left to the courts. The new government would do well to focus on development rather than on settling political scores.
